notes: Executable packages are installed into an application-local tools directory and never written into Windows system folders.
Large reference databases are intentionally managed separately because their releases, licences and storage requirements vary.
Native Windows packages are preferred when official binaries exist; Linux-first packages use the optional WSL/Bioconda backend.
Step 96 records executable versions, hashes, commands, stdout, stderr and exit codes for audited specialist-tool runs.
Step 100 expands audited detection for polishing, phylogenomics, pathogen typing and pooled-CRISPR tools without claiming they are bundled.
Step 120 adds audited readiness for epigenomics, GWAS, structural variation, splicing, mass spectrometry, antibody and imaging engines; proprietary/licensed engines remain operator-supplied.
